kitDescription: Signal is a Fire SMG Attacker with a Burst II on a 20-second cooldown. Her Skill 1 counts her own normal attacks and, every 60 landed rounds, briefly cuts the boss's DEF and ATK by 5.94% for 5 seconds — effectively permanent uptime while she keeps firing. Her Skill 2 triggers whenever the team enters Full Burst (from any caster, not just her own) and heals her for 44.08% of her attack damage over the following 10 seconds — a self-sustain tool with no damage role. Her Burst is an instant hit on all enemies in range for 229.22% of her final ATK, plus a 12.34% DEF cut on the boss for 10 seconds, so roughly half-uptime on a 20-second rotation. In game terms her team value is the recurring DEF shred; at this sim's scope (boss DEF ≈ 0, no incoming damage) both the DEF/ATK debuffs and the lifesteal are structurally inert, leaving the burst nuke as her only damage-relevant kit line.

skill1.driverSaid: Verbatim unmodeled + ⚑1 (estimate ~8.3 flat boss DEF at near-permanent uptime; recipe = debuff-scalable boss-DEF channel; tier engine-gap/minor); absence pinned against a damageTakenPct-laundering counterfactual that DOES emit and lift totals.
skill1.blindSaid: S2b: FAITHFUL conditional on an enemy-DEF consumer existing, with an explicit escape clause ('if the engine has no enemy-DEF consumer, the dispositions become GAP and the driver must declare that openly'). S6: encodes dead blocks whose own audit admits engine-inert. S5: expects dead blocks + events (5 REDs).
skill1.formulaCheck: SSOT §1a: boss DEF is a small flat subtractive term, run at bossDef:0 with no debuff-scalable channel; sim.ts enemyBuffs admits only damageTakenPct/distributedDamagePct > 0. The driver's declared GAP is exactly the S2b escape-clause branch, verified against engine dispatch. A damageTakenPct substitution would be the documented naming-trap fudge (DEF-subtractive ≠ Taken-multiplicative) — correctly refused by all parties.
skill1.explanation: Behaviorally identical across all three derivations (zero buffApply, zero total movement); the divergence is documentation policy — verbatim-unmodeled+flag vs dead blocks that emit nothing. The driver's treatment is the sanctioned one: the SSOT (game-mechanics.md 'Skill resolution') names `unmodeled` as the deliberate-skip channel, and encoding a trigger with effects the engine provably drops would be noise plus a false implication of observability. The S5 REDs on this line are a blind misread of engine behavior (it assumed dead encodings emit boss-debuff events; dispatch drops them), not a faithfulness signal — the blind's own mechanical fudge-detector ('shred moves NO damage') is GREEN against the driver override.

skill1.blindSaid: S2b: UNMODELED (no damage-side consumer). S6: encodes for completeness, self-flagged 'permanently 0 damage'. S5: presence-or-recorded check (its recorded-unmodeled branch passes).

skill1.explanation: Full three-way convergence on unmodeled; recorded verbatim. No gotcha.

skill2.driverSaid: fullBurstEnter → self → heal ticks:10 intervalSec:1; discriminated against burstCast keying by recovery start offset (every shipped firing strictly after the cast frame; counterfactual fires exactly ON every cast frame).
skill2.blindSaid: S2b: fullBurstEnter is 'the correct WIDER trigger; do not narrow it to burstCast'. S6: identical block, 'literal text, NOT burstCast'. S5 structural assertions on trigger/target GREEN.
skill2.formulaCheck: SSOT §8 + game-mechanics §9: 'when entering Full Burst' lines fire on the FB-entry event from any caster; the engine's fullBurstEnter trigger is the named primitive. Three-way convergence.
skill2.explanation: Fires on every team Full Burst (≥6 windows/180s observed via probe). The probe methodology is sound: the engine emits no recovery SimEvent and fireRecovery dispatches only the recipient's blocks, so a self-heal's window is observable only through the recipient's own recovery trigger; the probe (recovery → self defPct 1) is pinned damage-inert (probed totals byte-equal to base), matching the ether shield-probe precedent. Window shape (≥8 firings spanning ≥8s per window) distinguishes the 10s HoT from an instant heal; the counterfactual pins trigger identity. Cluster 2 RULED FAITHFUL.

skill2.driverSaid: Magnitude 44.08 verbatim in unmodeled.skill2 ('magnitude only — no HP pool by design'); the 10-second recovery-event window is the modeled substance (milk K6 / helm H8 precedent).

skill2.explanation: Magnitude gap is documented with the design reason; the encodable substance (event channel) is modeled and discriminated. No gotcha.

verdictRationale: No real gotchas. Every kit line is either FAITHFUL (S2 event channel, burst nuke) or a DOCUMENTED_GAP with estimate+recipe+tier (the three enemy ▼ lines — an engine-missing boss-DEF/ATK debuff channel — and the S2 44.08 magnitude, unmodelable without an HP pool). The three independent derivations converged on every encodable line: fullBurstEnter-not-burstCast on S2, burstCast + FB-exempt-by-cast-timing on the 229.22 nuke, and refusal to launder DEF▼ into damageTakenPct (the one fudge that would have moved totals, pinned RED by both driver and blind). The 7 S5 REDs decompose entirely into (a) a documentation-policy divergence the blind author's own mechanical assertions contradict — her fudge-detector is GREEN against the driver override, and the S6 blind's dead encodings are self-admittedly inert, so blind-vs-blind agrees the difference is policy not mechanics — and (b) the competing-B2 fixture artifact (crown takes every stage-2 cast; signal: 0 bursts), which vacates the blind nuke assertions under standing batch precedent; the driver's sole-B2 fixture pins the nuke non-vacuously. Ruling on Cluster 1: the driver's documented-zero treatment is faithful — verbatim unmodeled + flags is the SSOT-sanctioned skip channel, and dead blocks that provably emit nothing are noise that falsely implies observability; the dead encoding need NOT ship. Cluster 2: probe methodology and window assertions ruled faithful. Cluster 3: confirmed. Nothing must change for GO. Same-model residual for owner spot-check: (1) the ⚑ uptime/cadence estimates in flags 1-2 (near-permanent S1 uptime assumes ~24 hits/s SMG cadence — the SMG-rate question is owner-retired but the estimate is arithmetic on that premise); (2) all three agents are same-family-adjacent readers of the same prose, so a genuinely ambiguous English reading (none identified here — the kit is unusually literal) would converge falsely; the load-bearing facts (FB timing rule, enemyBuffs dispatch, heal event channel) are anchored in MEASURED SSOT entries, not shared priors.
